entry.title: News Summary: June 25, 2026

  • Qualcomm agreed to buy AI-software startup Modular for nearly $4 billion, expanding from edge devices into data centers
  • Blackstone committed $30 billion to AI data centers in Japan amid intensifying global buildout

entry.title: OpenAI and Broadcom announce chip designed for LLM inference at scale
entry.summary: OpenAI and Broadcom announced Jalapeno, a custom ASIC designed specifically for large language model inference in data centers. Both companies frame it as the first generation of a long-term silicon roadmap aimed at running models at scale.

entry.title: OpenAI unveils its first custom chip, built by Broadcom
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports OpenAI unveiled its first custom processor, Jalapeno, built with Broadcom and tailored for the specific demands of OpenAI inference systems. It marks OpenAI entry into bespoke AI silicon.

entry.title: OpenAI and Broadcom unveil LLM-optimized inference chip
entry.summary: OpenAI official announcement describes Jalapeno, a custom AI chip built with Broadcom and optimized for LLM inference to improve performance, efficiency, and scale. It represents OpenAI move into bespoke silicon.

entry.title: OpenAI and Broadcom unveil "Jalapeño," a custom chip built for LLM inference
entry.summary: The Decoder reports OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled the Jalapeno chip tailored for LLM inference, with plans to run it at scale by late 2026. It marks OpenAI adding custom hardware to its stack.

entry.title: Qualcomm Buys Buzzy Chip Startup Modular for Nearly $4 Billion
entry.summary: Qualcomm agreed to acquire AI chip software startup Modular for nearly 4 billion dollars, expanding from edge devices into data center infrastructure. Modular built one of the most prominent AI compiler and runtime stacks of the era.

entry.title: Qualcomm to Acquire AI Platform Developer Modular
entry.summary: Qualcomm announced it will acquire AI platform developer Modular, expanding its AI infrastructure ambitions from edge devices into data centers. The deal deepens Qualcomm push into the data-center AI stack.

entry.title: Blackstone Commits $30B as Japan’s AI Battle Heats Up
entry.summary: Blackstone committed 30 billion dollars to AI data center development in Japan as competition for AI infrastructure in the country intensifies. The plan joins a wave of multibillion-dollar data center deals.

entry.title: Agility Robotics plans to go public via SPAC in a $2.5B deal
entry.summary: Humanoid robotics startup Agility Robotics plans to go public via a SPAC in a 2.5 billion dollar deal expected to raise about 620 million dollars. The Oregon State spinout is targeting commercial scaling.

entry.title: Snowflake CEO finds GLM-5.2 competitive with Opus 4.7 at a fraction of the cost
entry.summary: Snowflake CEO reported that Zhipu AI GLM-5.2 nearly matched Claude Opus 4.7 on a 103-task coding benchmark at roughly one-fifth the cost per output token, though using nearly twice as many tokens. The result intensifies price pressure on Western labs.

entry.title: Claude Tag embeds Anthropic's AI in Slack, already writes 65 percent of internal code, company says
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the Claude Tag launch from yesterday, Anthropic launched Claude Tag, letting teams summon its AI in any Slack channel by tagging it and assigning tasks. The company says the tool already generates 65 percent of code on its product team.

entry.title: OpenAI reveals its first AI processor: Jalapeño
entry.summary: The Verge details OpenAI new Jalapeno ASIC, built with Broadcom for AI inference rather than training, arriving about nine months after the partnership was first revealed. The chip targets running ChatGPT and Codex agents at scale.

entry.title: OpenAI and Broadcom Introduce AI Inference Chip
entry.summary: Coverage notes OpenAI and Broadcom inference chip could let model makers offer lower token prices, potentially easing enterprise cost concerns. It frames Jalapeno as a lever on AI economics.

entry.title: DFlash Speculative Decoding Drafts Whole Token Blocks in Parallel for Up to 15x Higher Throughput on NVIDIA Blackwell
entry.summary: Researchers introduced DFlash, a block-diffusion speculative decoding method that drafts whole token blocks in parallel, reportedly achieving up to 15x higher throughput on NVIDIA Blackwell. It departs from the autoregressive drafting that caps prior methods near 2-3x.

entry.title: AI Is Designing Radio Chips That Humans Couldn’t Even Imagine
entry.summary: Princeton researchers used reinforcement learning, inverse design, and diffusion models to automatically generate radio-frequency integrated circuits, achieving record performance and slashing design time. The approach produces RF layouts humans would not conventionally devise.

entry.title: Introducing computer use in Gemini 3.5 Flash
entry.summary: Google DeepMind introduced computer use capabilities in Gemini 3.5 Flash, enabling the model to operate software interfaces. The addition extends agentic control to its fast, lower-cost model tier.

entry.title: AI researchers continue to leave Google for its rivals
entry.summary: Top Google AI researchers Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel are leaving for Anthropic, continuing a wave of departures that included Noam Shazeer and John Jumper. The exodus reflects intensifying talent competition.

entry.title: The $27 million Al proxy war over Alex Bores ends in a draw
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, The roughly 27 million dollar political proxy war between Anthropic and OpenAI ended in a draw as AI-safety advocate Alex Bores narrowly lost a New York primary. Bores had authored the RAISE Act imposing guardrails on frontier AI firms.

entry.title: Big tech spent millions on a single US congressional race. It won’t be the last time
entry.summary: More than 24 million dollars poured into a New York congressional primary as pro- and anti-AI groups fought a proxy battle, much of it targeting AI-safety bill sponsor Alex Bores. The race became a test of the AI industry political influence.

entry.title: Mistral's new OCR model beats competitors in 72 percent of blind test cases, company says
entry.summary: As first reported in News yesterday, Mistral released OCR 4, a document-reading model for PDFs, Word, and PowerPoint that the company says beats competitors in 72 percent of blind test cases. It adds features like bounding boxes for understanding unstructured data.

entry.title: Gradium Launches stt-translate and s2s-translate, Real-Time Speech Translation Models Beating gpt-realtime-translate on Accuracy and Latency
entry.summary: Gradium launched two real-time speech translation models, stt-translate and s2s-translate, covering five languages and 20 pairs while collapsing the usual three-model cascade into two. The company claims they beat gpt-realtime-translate and gemini-3.5-live-translate on accuracy and latency, adding voice cloning.

entry.title: [AINews] Claude Tag: Multiplayer, Proactive, Persistent Agents in Slack
entry.summary: An analysis of Anthropic Claude Tag frames it as a multiplayer, proactive, persistent agent living in Slack and a major iteration of the Claude interface. It notes the Tag form now merges 65 percent of Anthropic product pull requests.

entry.title: If an AI chatbot misleads you, who is to blame? | Bruce Schneier and Nathan E Sanders

author.name: Bruce Schneier and Nathan E Sanders

entry.summary: An opinion piece discusses a German court ruling that Google is liable for what its AI search summaries say, rejecting the defense that users should not trust AI blindly. The authors argue this accountability is overdue.

entry.title: Mistral AI Tackles Unstructured Data Challenge with OCR 4
entry.summary: Mistral released OCR 4 to tackle unstructured-data extraction, adding features such as bounding boxes to help users interpret document layouts. The model targets PDFs and office files.

entry.title: AI helps read papyrus scroll burnt to crisp during Vesuvius eruption
entry.summary: Researchers used AI to virtually unwrap and read a charred Herculaneum scroll, revealing 20 columns of previously hidden Stoic philosophical text without physically opening it. The work demonstrates AI-enabled recovery of ancient damaged manuscripts.

entry.title: ‘We should be worried’: report sheds light on ICE’s booming arsenal of hi-tech surveillance tools
entry.summary: A new report finds US government spending on AI-powered immigration surveillance soared to a record 513 million dollars in 2026, up sharply from prior years. Contracts with eleven surveillance tech firms doubled over the period.

entry.title: I Met With China’s Top AI Experts. They’re Freaking Out, Too
entry.summary: A feature reports that Chinese AI researchers share US counterparts fears about an uncontrolled arms race, raising the specter of a catastrophic incident. It highlights interest in cross-border cooperation on safety.

entry.title: OpenAI's deployment chief on Codex growth, falling AI prices, and the ROI question
entry.summary: OpenAI deployment chief discussed explosive Codex growth, a feedback loop from enterprise customers into model development, and a sharp drop in the price of AI intelligence. He outlined a strategy of embedding OpenAI engineers deep inside large corporations.

entry.title: Cerebras stock plunges after earnings as CEO says margin outlook was misunderstood
entry.summary: AI chipmaker Cerebras saw its stock fall after its first earnings report since going public, as a narrower forecast gross margin spooked investors. The CEO said the margin outlook was misunderstood.

entry.title: The Trump White House Is Over Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei
entry.summary: Reporting indicates the Trump White House has sidelined Anthropic cofounder Dario Amodei in high-stakes meetings, replacing him with cofounder Tom Brown. The shift signals strained relations between a leading AI lab and the administration.

entry.title: ‘Who is going to pay us when we’re replaced by robots?’ The Indian factory workers told to film themselves for AI
entry.summary: Indian garment factory workers were made to wear head-mounted cameras to capture footage for AI training, raising fears about job displacement and consent. The report exposes how low-wage labor feeds AI and robotics datasets.

entry.title: Nous Research Adds /learn to Hermes Agent’s Skills System, Capturing Workflows as Slash Commands Without Hand-Writing SKILL.md
entry.summary: Nous Research added a /learn command to its open-source Hermes Agent skills system, letting the agent author reusable SKILL.md files automatically from docs, code, conversations, or notes. It removes the need to hand-write skill definitions.

entry.title: Meta pauses employee tracker for AI training amid privacy concerns
entry.summary: Meta paused a tool that tracked employees keystrokes, mouse clicks, and screen content to gather AI training data after about 1,600 workers petitioned against it. The reversal followed privacy and surveillance concerns.

entry.title: Companies are scrambling to stop employees from maxing out AI budgets with small tasks
entry.summary: Companies are introducing controls to stop employees from exhausting AI budgets on trivial tasks, shifting from heavy token usage toward token rationing. The trend reflects rising scrutiny of AI cost-per-task ROI.

entry.title: Why the Frontier Ecosystem must be Open — Matei Zaharia and Reynold Xin, Databricks
entry.summary: Databricks cofounders Matei Zaharia and Reynold Xin discuss why frontier AI ecosystems must remain open, covering their Omnigent, Lakebase, and Mosaic efforts to extend the company into a full data-and-AI operating system for the agent era. They argue for open formats and agent security.

entry.title: Met gets extension to Palantir AI project after Sadiq Khan blocked deal
entry.summary: The Metropolitan Police received a 12-month extension on a Palantir pilot after the London mayor blocked a 50 million pound deal to automate criminal intelligence analysis. The force continues procurement for a long-term supplier.

entry.title: Figma adds code layers, support for animations, more AI features in new update
entry.summary: Figma's Config 2026 update adds code layers for editing project code on the canvas, AI-generated motion graphics and shader tools, and the ability to build custom plugins via AI. The release pushes Figma toward full-stack design-to-development workflows.

entry.title: OpenAI says ChatGPT Instant now better understands what users actually want
entry.summary: OpenAI updated GPT-5.5 Instant, its most-used ChatGPT model, to improve intent recognition, multi-turn context, and handling of complex multi-condition prompts. The update focuses on conversation quality rather than new capabilities.

entry.title: Figma now has AI motion graphics and shader tools
entry.summary: At Config 2026, Figma introduced a development-optimized canvas plus AI motion graphics and shader generation driven by natural-language prompts. Code layers let users edit project code without leaving the design canvas.

entry.title: A24 Knows You’re Mad About the Google AI Collab
entry.summary: Google DeepMind invested 75 million dollars in indie studio A24, drawing backlash from film fans worried about AI deepening its grip on Hollywood. The deal reflects accelerating AI-entertainment industry entanglement.

entry.title: Congresswoman denies staff used AI to write defense funding amendment
entry.summary: A US congresswoman denied that her staff used AI to draft a defense bill amendment after a leaked summary appeared to contain a Claude chatbot response, saying AI was used only for spellcheck. The episode highlights scrutiny of AI in legislative drafting.

entry.title: Pangram CEO says language models give themselves away by making the same arguments
entry.summary: Pangram CEO argues that language models reveal themselves by producing clustered, repetitive arguments when asked to brainstorm, whereas human reasoning is more diverse. The claim suggests a new angle for AI-text detection.

entry.title: Introducing the FFASR Leaderboard: Benchmarking ASR in the Real World
entry.summary: Hugging Face introduced the FFASR leaderboard for benchmarking automatic speech recognition under real-world conditions. It aims to evaluate ASR systems beyond clean-lab settings.

entry.title: Facebook rolls out an AI companion app for creators
entry.summary: Facebook is testing a standalone AI companion app for creators that incorporates its recently launched AI creator assistant. The app is being trialed with a select group of creators.

entry.title: Figma bets on human judgment at Config 2026 while the AI powering its canvas belongs to someone else
entry.summary: At Config 2026, Figma turned its canvas into a full workspace with code, animation, shaders, and AI agents. But the intelligence powering all of it is rented from API providers, squeezing mar...

entry.title: How to Design an OpenHarness Style Agent Runtime with Tools, Memory, Permissions, Skills, and Multi-Agent Coordination
entry.summary: A tutorial walks through building an OpenHarness-style agent runtime from scratch, covering tool use, typed schemas, permissions, memory, skills, context compaction, retries, cost tracking, and multi-agent coordination. It exposes the full control flow of an agent harness.

entry.title: How to Opt Out of Google Search’s New AI Data Training Feature
entry.summary: Google Search now stores media uploads from interactions, such as images used in reverse image search, for AI model training, and the article explains how to opt out. The change extends Google data collection deeper into search behavior.

entry.title: ‘You can’t make billions without hurting people’: Cory Doctorow on Elon Musk, the AI bubble and bosses’ cruel fantasies
entry.summary: Author Cory Doctorow argues in an interview that AI will not deliver on its promises and primarily appeals to those seeking to deskill and control labor, introducing his reverse centaur concept. The piece critiques the AI bubble and tech power.

entry.title: Accelerating Transformers Fine-Tuning with NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel
entry.summary: A Hugging Face and NVIDIA blog details accelerating Transformer fine-tuning using NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel. It targets faster, more efficient model customization workflows.

entry.title: Critic of Labor’s tax changes deletes anti-immigration AI video reposted from rightwing nationalist account
entry.summary: An Australian fund manager deleted an AI-generated anti-immigration video he had reposted from a far-right account after backlash. The incident underscores how generative AI fuels political disinformation.

entry.title: Huntington Bank: Redacting sensitive data from 400M+ documents with AWS
entry.summary: An AWS case study describes how Huntington Bank used Amazon services to systematically find and redact sensitive customer data across more than 400 million stored documents. The solution handles varied formats at high throughput.

entry.title: Build a healthcare appointment agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic
entry.summary: An AWS tutorial shows how to build a voice-based healthcare appointment agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic and Bedrock AgentCore that authenticates patients, manages bookings, collects pre-visit info, and escalates to staff. It targets reducing no-show rates.

entry.title: How Loka Built a Natural, Low-Latency Voice Agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic
entry.summary: An AWS case study describes how Loka built a low-latency conversational voice agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic that improves speech reasoning accuracy while cutting cost and latency versus traditional pipelines. It avoids the multi-step speech-to-text cascade.

entry.title: 16 Best Generative AI Coding Tools in 2026 Compared: Features, and Best Fit
entry.summary: A roundup compares 16 generative AI coding tools for 2026, spanning autocomplete, multi-agent build pipelines, and natural-language interfaces to entire codebases. It aims to help engineers pick tools by task fit.

entry.title: AI-powered BI with Snowflake and Amazon Quick
entry.summary: An AWS post explains using Amazon Quick Sight on Snowflake semantic views to reconcile inconsistent business metrics across dashboards and chat agents. It addresses the last-mile gap where business logic lives in apps rather than the data layer.

entry.title: The emergence of the web data infrastructure layer for AI
entry.summary: A sponsored piece argues that AI demand is driving the emergence of a new web data infrastructure layer enabling models to discover and retrieve information across billions of URLs. It frames structured web access as the next AI frontier.

entry.title: OpenAI says new GPT-5.5-Cyber outperforms Anthropic's Mythos on cybersecurity benchmark
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of OpenAI's cyber push from yesterday, OpenAI released the full GPT-5.5-Cyber model and an updated Codex Security plugin under its Daybreak initiative, claiming it beats Anthropic's Mythos on a cybersecurity benchmark. The program adds 25-plus security partners and shifts emphasis from finding vulnerabilities to automatically patching them.

entry.title: ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 breaks the 30-second barrier for AI video generation
entry.summary: ByteDance unveiled five new AI models at its FORCE conference, headlined by Seedance 2.5, a video generator said to surpass the 30-second clip barrier and slated for an early-July launch. The duration breakthrough pushes the frontier of AI video generation.

entry.title: [AINews] SpaceX is already a $28B/yr Neocloud
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's coverage of the SpaceX–Reflection AI deal, A roundup highlights SpaceX emerging as roughly a 28 billion dollar per year neocloud GPU rental business, having signed a third GPU deal with Reflection AI alongside Anthropic and Google. It also notes Baseten's confirmed 13 billion dollar Series F and assorted news across OpenAI Daybreak, Gemini, and Sakana Fugu.

entry.title: Anthropic’s Claude Tag is learning your company, one Slack message at a time
entry.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Tag, an always-on agentic AI teammate that integrates into company Slack channels to absorb organizational context and execute delegated tasks. Anthropic frames it as an evolution of Claude Code aimed at capturing enterprise workflows and institutional knowledge.

entry.title: Cursor announces its own AI model, a new Git platform, and a mobile app
entry.summary: Cursor revealed its first fully in-house trained AI coding model along with a new Git platform and a mobile app. The vertical move reduces Cursor's reliance on third-party model providers.

entry.title: US AI stock sell-off shakes markets from Wall Street to Asia
entry.summary: A broad tech sell-off pushed the Nasdaq down 2.2 percent as investors questioned elevated AI valuations and heavy infrastructure spending. Losses spread from Wall Street to Asian markets.

entry.title: Sakana AI's Fugu orchestrates multiple LLMs to match Anthropic's Fable and Mythos benchmarks
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of Sakana's Fugu launch from yesterday, Sakana AI launched Fugu, a system that orchestrates multiple LLMs on the fly to match the benchmark performance of Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos. The approach is positioned to reduce dependence on any single AI provider.

entry.title: Prime Intellect Releases prime-rl 0.6.0 to Train Trillion-Parameter MoE Models on Agentic RL Workloads
entry.summary: Prime Intellect released prime-rl 0.6.0, an open framework for reinforcement learning on trillion-parameter MoE models targeting long-horizon agentic workloads. It reportedly trained GLM-5 on software-engineering tasks at 131k sequence length with sub-five-minute steps on only 28 H200 nodes.

entry.title: Oracle’s 21,000 layoffs help drive its debt-fueled AI investments
entry.summary: An SEC filing revealed Oracle cut roughly 21,000 jobs over the year, a 12.9 percent workforce reduction, explicitly attributing some cuts to AI adoption and deployment. The company is reallocating resources toward debt-financed AI infrastructure investments.

entry.title: OpenAI launches new initiative to help find and patch open source bugs
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of OpenAI's open-source security initiative from yesterday, OpenAI launched an initiative, working with Trail of Bits, to use AI to find and patch vulnerabilities in open source software. The effort aims to strengthen the open source community's security posture.

entry.title: The $400 million machine powering the future of chipmaking
entry.summary: An in-depth feature profiles ASML's roughly 400 million dollar EUV lithography machine that underpins advanced chipmaking. The piece details the extreme engineering enabling the semiconductors that power AI.

entry.title: Mistral OCR 4 Brings Citation-Ready Structured Output to RAG, Agentic, and Enterprise Search Pipelines
entry.summary: Mistral released OCR 4, a document-understanding model adding bounding boxes, block classification, and per-word confidence scores across 170 languages, deployable in a single self-hosted container. Independent annotators preferred it over every tested system, averaging 72 percent win rates, at 4 dollars per 1,000 pages.

entry.title: Anthropic reimagines Claude in Slack as nosy, always-on agentic AI coworker
entry.summary: The Register details how Anthropic is retiring its existing Claude in Slack app for Claude Tag, an always-on agentic coworker that listens to and learns from whatever channels admins grant it. Anthropic frames it as the next step beyond Claude Code, with concerns raised about its pervasive data access.

entry.title: How GPT-5 helped immunologist Derya Unutmaz solve a 3-year-old mystery
entry.summary: OpenAI highlighted how GPT-5 Pro helped immunologist Derya Unutmaz resolve a three-year-old mystery about T cell behavior. The insight could aid cancer and autoimmune research.

entry.title: Why corporate AI super PACs spent $27 million on a local election
entry.summary: A newsletter examines why corporate AI super PACs poured 27 million dollars into a single New York local election involving Alex Bores. It highlights the growing political spending power of AI-aligned interests.

entry.title: Getty Images Enters Into Content Deal With OpenAI
entry.summary: Getty Images signed a content licensing deal with OpenAI as its stock has fallen sharply amid the rise of generative AI. The agreement reflects ongoing realignment between stock-image providers and AI developers.

entry.title: Datalab Releases lift: A 9B Open-Weights Vision Model That Extracts Structured JSON From PDFs Using Schemas
entry.summary: Datalab released lift, a 9B open-weights vision model that extracts schema-conforming structured JSON directly from PDFs and images. It scores 90.2 percent field accuracy on the company's 225-document benchmark at about 9.5 seconds per document.

entry.title: Helping build shared standards for advanced AI
entry.summary: OpenAI described its work supporting shared standards for advanced AI through the Appia Foundation, including evaluation frameworks, safety practices, and global cooperation. The post frames it as contributing to international AI governance.

entry.title: Majority of datacenters are vulnerable to climate threats like floods and fires, study finds
entry.summary: A First Street report found nearly 80 percent of datacenters are exposed to climate hazards such as flooding, extreme wind, and wildfires, raising risks of downtime and higher insurance costs. The finding underscores a feedback loop between AI's emissions and the infrastructure those emissions threaten.

entry.title: Australia ‘sleepwalking’ into AI crisis and ‘tech bro free-for-all’, says Greens senator
entry.summary: Australian senators are pressing the government to block tech firms from training AI on Australian content and to pause new datacenter approvals until regulation catches up. The calls come as cabinet weighs copyright rule changes for AI.

entry.title: Meta launches cheaper smart glasses without Ray-Ban
entry.summary: Meta launched its own line of smart glasses independent of the Ray-Ban partnership, including a cheaper model and a Kylie Jenner collaboration across multiple styles and colors. The move expands Meta's standalone presence in the AI wearables market.

entry.title: AI Is Learning to Read the Room
entry.summary: An analysis examines emotion AI's push toward context-aware affective computing that goes beyond simplistic happy/sad labels to infer nuanced states like stress and burnout. It raises questions about workplace use cases such as performance reviews.

entry.title: AI in the classroom prompts tide of concern from US parents and experts
entry.summary: US parents and education experts are voicing concern over the push, backed by tech firms and the Trump administration, to embed AI chatbots in classrooms. Critics argue there is little evidence AI improves learning and worry it erodes independent thinking.

entry.title: Something’s off with Midjourney’s pivot to body scanners
entry.summary: Midjourney, known for image generation, is pivoting into medical imaging with a futuristic water-immersion ultrasound scanner claimed to rival MRI. Medical imaging experts told The Verge the company has shown little evidence supporting its claims.

entry.title: How AI is Reshaping Europe's Digital Sovereignty Debate
entry.summary: A commentary explores strategies for European governments to pursue AI sovereignty amid the digital sovereignty debate. The piece is high-level policy framing.

entry.title: Build a protein research copilot with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: An AWS technical post shows how to build a protein research copilot on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, combining natural language query parsing, vector similarity search over protein embeddings, and AI-generated summaries. It targets faster peptide similarity discovery for researchers.

entry.title: GLM-5.2 OpenAI-Compatible API: A Hands-On Guide to Reasoning Effort, Function Calling, and Long-Context Retrieval
entry.summary: A hands-on tutorial demonstrates using GLM-5.2's hosted OpenAI-compatible API for reasoning-effort control, function calling, structured output, and long-context retrieval. It builds a reusable client and small tool-using agent.

entry.title: You’re only supposed to blow the bloody hooves off: AI Michael Caine narrates Odyssey audiobook
entry.summary: ElevenLabs released an officially licensed AI voice replica of Michael Caine narrating a new audiobook of Homer's Odyssey. The launch highlights the growing market for sanctioned synthetic voice productions.

entry.title: The Fitbit Air takes a smarter approach to the AI health dumpster fire
entry.summary: A review of Google's Fitbit Air finds its AI Health Coach delivers a more measured, if mixed, experience than rival AI health products. It is positioned as one of the better attempts at an AI-enabled wearable.

entry.title: Shared infrastructure, isolated tenants: Pool model multi-tenancy with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: An AWS post details patterns for production multi-tenant AI applications using Bedrock AgentCore, emphasizing tenant isolation, service tiers, cost tracking, and per-tenant observability. It uses healthcare AI agents as the example domain.

entry.title: How to Use NVIDIA Canary-1B-v2 for ASR, Translation, and Automatic SRT Subtitle Export in Python
entry.summary: A tutorial walks through building an ASR, translation, and SRT subtitle pipeline using NVIDIA's Canary-1B-v2 model in Python. It covers setup, transcription, multilingual translation, and benchmarking.

entry.title: Experimenting with the proposed Cross-Origin Storage API in Transformers.js
entry.summary: A Hugging Face blog explores experimenting with the proposed Cross-Origin Storage API in Transformers.js. It addresses browser-side model storage for in-browser inference.

entry.title: How to burst the AI bubble: Strike at its roots
entry.summary: Cory Doctorow promotes a new book arguing against AI hype and what he frames as the technology's harmful labor and economic dynamics. The piece is a cultural critique rather than a technical development.

entry.title: Shipping huggingface_hub every week with AI, open tools, and a human in the loop
entry.summary: A Hugging Face engineering blog describes shipping weekly huggingface_hub releases using AI, open tooling, and human-in-the-loop review. It focuses on CI and release-process automation.

entry.title: Sony’s AI Camera Assistant is exactly as bad as it looks
entry.summary: A hands-on review concludes Sony's new AI Camera Assistant on the Xperia 1 VIII performs poorly, producing notably bad photography guidance. The reviewer found it worse than comparable features like Google's Camera Coach.

entry.title: ‘Navigating the unknown together’: me and my idiot AI boyfriend
entry.summary: A first-person essay recounts a skeptical writer's assigned experiment using an AI chatbot as a romantic companion. It is a personal reflection on the AI relationship phenomenon.

entry.title: News Summary: June 23, 2026
entry.summary:
AI cybersecurity led the day. The Five Eyes intelligence alliance issued a rare joint warning that frontier AI models capable of devastating cyberattacks on governments and businesses are months away.

entry.title: AI models capable of devastating attacks on governments and business months away, rare Five Eyes statement warns
entry.summary: Signals intelligence agencies of the Five Eyes alliance issued a rare joint public statement warning that AI models capable of devastating cyberattacks on governments and businesses are only months away, urging leaders to act. The warning follows the Trump administration blocking foreign nationals from Anthropic's Fable model.

entry.title: OpenAI Launches Full-Scale Effort to Patch Open-Source Bugs as It Takes on Anthropic’s Mythos
entry.summary: OpenAI unveiled an upgraded GPT-5.5-Cyber and a Patch the Planet initiative to find and fix open-source software vulnerabilities at scale, positioning itself against Anthropic's Mythos amid rising concern over AI cyber capabilities. The move pairs offensive-grade model abilities with defensive remediation programs.

entry.title: Sakana AI Launches Sakana Fugu: An Orchestration Model That Routes Tasks Across a Swappable Pool of Frontier LLMs
entry.summary: Sakana AI launched Fugu, a multi-agent orchestration system that behaves as a single model behind one OpenAI-compatible API, routing tasks across a swappable pool of frontier LLMs. Sakana claims its Fugu Ultra leads most published coding and reasoning benchmarks and outperforms the individual models it coordinates.

entry.title: Five Eyes intelligence alliance says frontier AI models could reshape offensive cyber ops in months
entry.summary: The Decoder relays the Five Eyes alliance's warning that frontier AI models could reshape offensive cyber operations within months, echoing the joint intelligence statement. It reinforces the urgency framing from signals agencies.

entry.title: AI chipmaker Groq confirms $650M raise, re-staffs after Nvidia’s $20B not-acqui-hire deal
entry.summary: AI chipmaker Groq confirmed a $650M raise and is re-staffing its executive ranks, doubling down on its neocloud business after an unusual $20B Nvidia not-acqui-hire arrangement. The company is repositioning around inference infrastructure.

entry.title: Patch the Planet: a Daybreak initiative to support open source maintainers
entry.summary: OpenAI announced Patch the Planet, a Daybreak initiative to help open-source maintainers find, validate, and fix vulnerabilities using AI plus expert review. It pairs automated discovery with human oversight to harden widely used open-source code.

entry.title: New York City House primary emerges as key battleground in ‘AI civil war’
entry.summary: AI-focused Super PACs have raised over $100M for the 2026 midterms, with nearly half of all spending so far concentrated on a single Manhattan congressional primary. The race is being framed as a battleground in an emerging political fight over how AI will be regulated.

entry.title: Anthropic and Micron want to co-design AI memory architecture
entry.summary: Micron is investing in Anthropic's Series H round and signed a multi-year deal to supply and co-design memory for Claude's infrastructure, which Anthropic calls critical to training and serving its models. Critics warn such circular supplier-investor deals are inflating an AI bubble, noting Micron's stock has surged more than tenfold in a year.

entry.title: People training new AI models admit they just get chatbots to do it
entry.summary: New Scientist reports that human workers hired to train next-generation models by conversing with them are instead using chatbots to do the work. Experts warn this 'AI inbreeding' could degrade the quality and usefulness of future models.

entry.title: How Anthropic may have talked itself into an AI export ban
entry.summary: An FT analysis finds Anthropic uses risk and regulation language roughly eight times more frequently than OpenAI, and critics argue this rhetoric helped trigger the US government's ban on foreign access to its Mythos and Fable models. The piece frames Anthropic's safety messaging as having backfired into a regulatory crackdown on its own products.

entry.title: SpaceX inks compute deal with Reflection AI, an open source AI lab
entry.summary: SpaceX struck a deal for open-source lab Reflection AI to pay $150M per month from mid-2026 through 2029 for access to Nvidia GB300 chips and supporting hardware at SpaceX's Colossus 2 data center near Memphis. The arrangement reflects the scale of compute commitments now flowing to AI labs.

entry.title: Daybreak: Tools for securing every organization in the world
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced Daybreak, a suite of security tools including Codex Security and GPT-5.5-Cyber, to help organizations find, validate, and patch vulnerabilities at scale. It positions OpenAI's models as defensive cybersecurity infrastructure.

entry.title: Three things to watch amid Anthropic’s latest feud with the government
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review recaps and analyzes the Anthropic-government standoff over Mythos and Fable, explaining how Anthropic flagged the models as cyber threats before the government imposed export controls and the company revoked access. It outlines key dynamics to watch in the dispute.

entry.title: Google DeepMind bets $75M on AI’s future in Hollywood with A24 deal
entry.summary: Google DeepMind is partnering with film studio A24 and investing roughly $75M to develop AI filmmaking tools. The deal signals deeper integration of generative AI into Hollywood production workflows.

entry.title: Google Deepmind and A24 team up on AI filmmaking research
entry.summary: The Decoder confirms Google DeepMind and A24 are forming a long-term AI filmmaking research partnership, with Google investing about $75M in the studio per the Wall Street Journal. It frames a deepening lab-studio collaboration on creative AI.

entry.title: World Model AI Lab Odyssey Now Valued at $1.45B
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz around world models, World-model startup Odyssey is now valued at $1.45B, joining a cohort of well-funded labs building physical/world-model AI. The valuation signals strong investor appetite for spatial and physical-AI systems.

entry.title: MoonMath AI Open-Sources a HIP Attention Kernel for AMD MI300X That Beats AITER v3 on Every Shape and Rounding Mode
entry.summary: MoonMath AI open-sourced an MIT-licensed bf16 forward attention kernel for AMD's MI300X GPU, written in HIP rather than assembly, reporting it beats AMD's own AITER v3 kernel on every tested shape and rounding mode (up to 1.26x). The work targets better AMD-based AI compute performance.

entry.title: HR consultant wins English court case using AI lawyer in apparent legal first
entry.summary: An AI law firm, Garfield AI, reportedly won a debt-recovery case in an English court for roughly £400, in what is believed to be the first trial won using AI-generated legal material. The barrister stressed that courtroom advocacy itself remained human.

entry.title: Google makes Interactions API the default interface for Gemini models and agents
entry.summary: Google DeepMind has made its Interactions API the default interface for Gemini models and agents, replacing the older generateContent API with a simplified, typed-step schema. New agent features will ship only through this interface going forward.

entry.title: Red-Teaming after Mythos — Zico Kolter & Matt Fredrikson, Gray Swan
entry.summary: A Latent.Space discussion with Zico Kolter and Matt Fredrikson of Gray Swan examines red-teaming, jailbreaks, and indirect prompt injection in the wake of the Mythos export-control action. Gray Swan was cited on the Mythos model card and investigated its capabilities.

entry.title: Getty Images strikes multi-year deal to put licensed photos in ChatGPT search
entry.summary: Getty Images signed a multi-year licensing agreement with OpenAI to supply licensed photographs for use in ChatGPT search. The deal reflects continued movement toward licensed content in AI products.

entry.title: Nvidia Launches System to Make Robots Safer
entry.summary: Nvidia launched a system to improve robot safety, applying its autonomous-vehicle safety expertise to physical AI. The platform targets safer deployment of robotics in real-world environments.

entry.title: The AI world is getting ‘loopy’
entry.summary: TechCrunch describes an emerging shift toward continuous 'loops' of autonomous agent swarms that work endlessly in the background, extending agentic AI beyond single-task execution. The framing highlights a new operating paradigm for always-on autonomous agents.

entry.title: Anthropic Aims to Transform Enterprise Collaboration With Artifacts
entry.summary: Anthropic is pushing its Artifacts feature toward enterprise collaboration, reflecting a broader trend of AI labs moving beyond raw models into hosted services that resemble cloud providers. The shift emphasizes platform and workflow lock-in.

entry.title: Nvidia says its AI data center design runs hotter to use a lot less water
entry.summary: Nvidia is promoting its Rubin-generation reference design for fully liquid-cooled data centers, claiming it eliminates nearly all water use and large amounts of power consumption. Critics note it does not address construction impacts or upstream power-generation demands, and Nvidia omits cost comparisons.

entry.title: PP-OCRv6 on Hugging Face: 50-Language OCR from 1.5M to 34.5M Parameters
entry.summary: PaddlePaddle released PP-OCRv6 on Hugging Face, an OCR family supporting 50 languages with models ranging from 1.5M to 34.5M parameters. The compact open release targets efficient multilingual text recognition.

entry.title: Nvidia wants to cut data center water use, but that’s not the same as fixing AI’s water problem
entry.summary: Nvidia announced a cooling system that reduces water use inside data centers, but TechCrunch argues it sidesteps AI's larger water footprint from fossil-fuel power generation. The piece distinguishes on-site efficiency from total environmental impact.

entry.title: Read this before you vibe-code another app
entry.summary: The Verge examines security risks in vibe-coded applications, illustrating how non-experts ship AI-generated apps with vulnerabilities like SQL injection. It serves as a cautionary look at the downstream security debt of casual AI coding.

entry.title: xAI Launches /goal in Grok Build, Adding Long-Running Autonomous Execution With Built-In Verification for Multi-Step Coding Tasks
entry.summary: xAI added a /goal mode to its Grok Build terminal coding agent, enabling long-running autonomous execution that plans, builds a checklist, executes, and self-verifies tasks until completion. Verification can include code review, webpage inspection, or running scripts.

entry.title: Building pay-per-intelligence for AI agents: How Ampersend uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments
entry.summary: An AWS post details how Ampersend built a pay-per-intelligence routing layer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments, letting autonomous agents transact programmatically using protocols like x402 without bespoke billing integrations. It addresses how agents pay for services within governed limits.

entry.title: Meta Exposed Data Internally From Its Controversial Employee-Tracking Program
entry.summary: Meta accidentally exposed employee keystroke data internally that had been collected as part of a controversial program to train AI models on workers' typing behavior. Employees had previously objected to the surveillance initiative.

entry.title: Amazon is testing Alexa+ in India with Hindi support
entry.summary: Amazon is expanding its conversational assistant Alexa+ into India and inviting users to test a Hindi-language version. The move extends its generative voice assistant to a major new market.

entry.title: AI is cursing renters with the promise of impossible homes
entry.summary: The Verge reports on how AI-generated virtual staging of rental listings is misleading prospective tenants with images of apartments that don't match reality. The piece documents consumer harm from synthetic real-estate imagery.

entry.title: Embed the world: Multimodal AI for searchable aerial imagery at scale
entry.summary: An AWS engineering post describes building a natural-language-searchable index of aerial imagery at scale using multimodal embeddings, LLM captioning, and vector search, developed with imagery provider Vexcel. It presents an index-once, query-by-language approach to geospatial data.

entry.title: Running ComfyUI workflows on Amazon SageMaker AI processing jobs
entry.summary: An AWS how-to explains running ComfyUI media-generation workflows on Amazon SageMaker processing jobs to automate image, audio, and video content creation at scale. It targets enterprise marketing and campaign production.

entry.summary: At its New York summit, AWS launched two services targeting weaknesses in AI agents: Continuum, which detects and fixes code vulnerabilities automatically, and Context, which builds a knowledge graph from corporate data to ground agents. Both address agents that code quickly but make frequent errors.

entry.title: When the Trump administration cracks down on Anthropic, who benefits?
entry.summary: A TechCrunch Equity podcast episode examines the Trump administration's latest regulatory moves against Anthropic and what triggered them. The discussion explores the broader implications for the AI ecosystem and which competitors might gain from the crackdown.

entry.title: Samsung Electronics brings ChatGPT and Codex to employees
entry.summary: Samsung Electronics is deploying ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to employees worldwide, in what OpenAI describes as one of its largest enterprise rollouts. The move signals deepening corporate adoption of OpenAI's coding and productivity tools at major manufacturers.

entry.title: AI is inflating student grades, and the effect points to outsourced work, not better learning
entry.summary: A UC Berkeley study of over 500,000 grades found that writing- and coding-heavy courses saw grades rise after ChatGPT launched. The effect concentrated in homework, suggesting students are outsourcing work to AI rather than learning more effectively.

entry.title: Sam Altman says a whole generation of researchers held AI back by underestimating what scaling could do
entry.summary: At a Stanford talk, Sam Altman defended LLM scaling and criticized skeptical researchers he says slowed progress by underestimating its potential. He pointed to OpenAI's recent disproof of a mathematical conjecture as supporting evidence.

entry.title: Beyond Siri: Here are the practical AI features coming to your iPhone in iOS 27
entry.summary: Apple is rolling out practical AI features across iOS 27 beyond the headline Siri overhaul revealed at WWDC. The piece highlights smaller, utility-focused Apple Intelligence capabilities spread through the operating system.

entry.title: The 7 Types of Agent Memory: A Technical Guide for AI Engineers
entry.summary: A technical guide for engineers outlines seven distinct types of agent memory, explaining how stateless LLMs can be augmented to retain context across reasoning steps. It categorizes memory by form and duration, spanning context windows, external databases, and model weights.

entry.summary: Nobel laureate John Jumper, a key figure behind AlphaFold, is reportedly leaving Google DeepMind for rival Anthropic, and is said to be one of several high-profile departures. The move signals intensifying talent competition among frontier labs, especially in AI for science.

entry.title: OpenAI tripled revenue to $5.7 billion in Q1 but burned through $3.7 billion to get there
entry.summary: OpenAI reportedly tripled year-over-year Q1 2026 revenue to about $5.7 billion while burning roughly $3.7 billion, with stock-based compensation exceeding $2.3 billion. The company holds about $73 billion in reserves but could face pressure if a price war with Anthropic intensifies.

entry.title: The UK will scan asylum-seekers’ faces for age checks—despite knowing the tech is flawed

author.name: Matt Burgess, Maddy Varner, May Bulman, Gabriel Geiger, WIRED.com

entry.summary: The UK plans to deploy facial age estimation AI at its border starting next year to assess the ages of asylum seekers, reportedly the first use of FAE in this context. Critics highlight that the government is proceeding despite acknowledged inaccuracies in the technology, raising civil liberties and reliability concerns.

entry.title: OpenAI's Codex can now watch you work once and repeat the task forever
entry.summary: OpenAI added a Record & Replay feature to its macOS Codex app, letting users demonstrate a workflow once so Codex can convert it into a reusable skill and repeat it autonomously. The feature is not yet available in the EU, UK, or Switzerland.

entry.title: The Atlantic created a searchable database of the music used to train AI
entry.summary: The Atlantic's Alex Reisner identified four music datasets used to train AI, two containing roughly 12 million and 9 million tracks, and made them publicly searchable. Google and Stability have confirmed usage in research papers, intensifying scrutiny over copyrighted training data.

entry.title: Siri AI Hands On: A Smart, Helpful Assistant
entry.summary: Wired offers a hands-on review of the revamped Siri, describing it as conversational, omnipresent, and genuinely useful, with tags suggesting Google Gemini involvement under the hood. The piece frames Apple's assistant as finally competitive after years of lagging.

entry.title: Data2Story turns a CSV file into a verified interactive news article using seven AI agents
entry.summary: Researchers from Oxford and Stanford built Data2Story, a system of seven coordinated AI agents that converts a CSV into a finished interactive news article with graphics, web research, and source links for 93 percent of statements. In a reader study 74 percent preferred the agent output over the human original, though it only tied against elaborate long-form reports.

entry.title: The EU doesn't really know what a deepfake is, and that's becoming a problem for retail
entry.summary: Eurocommerce, representing retailers like Amazon, H&M, and IKEA, is lobbying for AI-generated ads to be exempt from EU AI Act transparency rules, arguing a synthetic product image is not a deepfake. The dispute exposes ambiguity in the law's definitions, with Zalando saying 90 percent of its marketing content is already AI-generated.

entry.title: NYU finance professor Damodaran warns an AI crash could hit harder than the dot-com bust
entry.summary: NYU finance professor Aswath Damodaran argues a potential AI crash could be worse than the dot-com bust because the sector is building heavily debt-financed physical infrastructure rather than light software. He also warns that even successful AI carries societal risk by aiming to replace whole jobs.

entry.title: Cisco AI Introduces FAPO: Pipeline-Aware Prompt Optimization With Step-Level Failure Attribution and Claude Code Orchestration
entry.summary: Cisco AI released FAPO (Fully Automated Prompt Optimization), an open-source Apache 2.0 system orchestrated by Claude Code agents that iteratively optimizes LLM pipelines from baseline prompts toward target accuracy. It adds step-level failure attribution to pinpoint failing stages in multi-step pipelines and also supports Codex.

entry.title: Signal’s Meredith Whittaker wants you to remember that AI chatbots ‘are not your friends’
entry.summary: Signal president Meredith Whittaker warns that AI chatbots are neither friends, conscious, nor sentient, pushing back against anthropomorphic framing and emotional dependence on assistants. The remarks emphasize privacy and the commercial incentives behind companion-style AI.

entry.title: ChatGPT keeps creeping toward becoming your AI personal assistant with new scheduled task controls
entry.summary: OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT's scheduling capabilities with a dedicated Scheduled page to view, pause, edit, or delete tasks, plus research tasks that alert users only on meaningful changes. The previous Pulse feature is being retired in the process.

entry.title: A viral doomsday scenario aims to shake Europe out of its AI complacency
entry.summary: A viral thought-experiment imagines a 2031 in which the US and China dominate AI while Europe falls behind on datacenters, robotics, and workflow automation. The Guardian examines whether the scenario reflects genuine strategic risk or merely anxiety about US tech ascendancy.

entry.title: Nous Research Updates Hermes Agent With a Blank Slate Mode That Pins Toolsets via platform_toolsets.cli and disabled_toolsets
entry.summary: Nous Research added a Blank Slate mode to its open-source Hermes Agent that boots with nearly all toolsets disabled except model, file operations, and terminal, and pins the surface so skipped capabilities never load later. It joins existing Quick Setup and Full Setup options for the self-improving, locally run agent.

entry.title: How to Build a Forecasting Pipeline with TimeCopilot Using Foundation Models and Automated Anomaly Detection
entry.summary: A tutorial demonstrates building an end-to-end forecasting pipeline with TimeCopilot, combining statistical, foundation, and GPU-based models with rolling cross-validation, probabilistic forecasts, and anomaly detection. It also showcases an optional LLM agent that selects models and explains predictions in natural language.

entry.title: In the Weights is your new AI-centric vanity search
entry.summary: A new tool called In the Weights lets users generate an AI-centric vanity score, a lighthearted measure of one's presence or footprint in AI systems. The launch is positioned as a novelty rather than a serious analytics product.

entry.title: [AINews] not much happened today
entry.summary: The Latent Space AI newsletter reports a quiet news day, noting that GLM 5.2 continues to trend strongly, alongside promotion for the AIE WF 2026 conference and subscriber ticket discounts. No substantive new development is detailed.

entry.title: A startup claims it broke through a bottleneck that’s holding back LLMs
entry.summary: Miami startup Subquadratic claims its new SubQ model solves a long-standing mathematical bottleneck, running faster, cheaper, and more energy-efficiently while processing up to 12x more text at once. An independent evaluation reportedly lends some credibility to the bold claims.

entry.title: OpenAI researchers show small doses of "beneficial trait" training make AI models broadly safer and harder to manipulate
entry.summary: OpenAI researchers report that reinforcement learning on small amounts of desired behavioral traits like truthfulness and corrigibility generalizes broadly, making models safer and harder to manipulate. Training on health data even improved deception detection, with gains on 44 of 53 benchmarks, in contrast to Anthropic's constitution-based approach.

entry.title: The US says ASML’s top chip tool may be in China, but how?
entry.summary: US officials suggest ASML's most advanced chipmaking tool may have reached China, though ASML disputes this, citing the commercial risk to its export license. The dispute touches the core of semiconductor export controls shaping AI compute.

entry.title: Is the US government’s Anthropic ban accidentally helping the brand?
entry.summary: A podcast segment examines whether the US government's forced withdrawal of Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models is inadvertently boosting the brand. Security researchers signed an open letter calling the move dangerous, and Anthropic noted the same jailbreaks exist in rival models.

entry.title: New benchmark exposes how badly AI struggles with real knowledge work
entry.summary: A new benchmark for realistic knowledge work shows even the best AI models fully solve just 3% of tasks, exposing significant gaps between hype and capability. The results challenge claims that agents are ready for complex professional work.

entry.title: NVIDIA AI Introduce SpatialClaw: A Training-Free Agent That Treats Code as the Action Interface for Spatial Reasoning
entry.summary: NVIDIA Research released SpatialClaw, a training-free agent that treats code as the action interface for spatial reasoning in vision-language models. It reaches 59.9% average accuracy across 20 benchmarks, outperforming the prior SpaceTools agent by 11.2 points without retraining.

entry.title: Billionaire Ambani wants AI in every call, app, and home
entry.summary: Reliance is integrating AI across telecom services reaching more than 500 million users, per Mukesh Ambani's plans to embed AI in every call, app, and home. The move represents one of the largest-scale consumer AI deployments globally.

entry.title: VibeThinker-3B: A 3B Dense Reasoning Model Built on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B With the Spectrum-to-Signal Post-Training Pipeline
entry.summary: Sina Weibo researchers released VibeThinker-3B, a 3B-parameter dense reasoning model built on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B using a spectrum-to-signal post-training pipeline. Under an MIT open-source license, it reportedly matches far larger models on math, coding, and STEM tasks.

entry.title: Google appeals ruling that made it directly liable for AI-generated search overview content
entry.summary: Google is appealing a Munich court ruling that held it directly liable for inaccurate AI search overviews after the system falsely linked two publishers to fraud schemes. Google characterizes the outputs as minor errors, but the court treated them as actionable harm.

entry.title: From PGP to Mythos: a brief history of export controls that didn’t stop anyone
entry.summary: Analysis argues that three decades of cyber-related export controls have failed to stop the spread of sensitive software, casting doubt on restrictions targeting Anthropic's Mythos cybersecurity model. The piece frames the Mythos controls as historically unlikely to be effective.

entry.title: Barret Zoph is out at OpenAI again after just five months
entry.summary: Barret Zoph, OpenAI's head of enterprise AI sales, has departed just five months after rejoining from Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab. His exit affects OpenAI's enterprise revenue push ahead of a planned IPO.

entry.title: Norway bans generative AI tools in elementary schools to protect kids' basic learning skills
entry.summary: Norway will ban generative AI tools in elementary schools (grades 1-7) from late August, with secondary use only under supervision, to protect foundational literacy and math skills. The prime minister argues children must first learn core skills before using AI.

entry.title: [AINews] GLM > GPT? GLM-5.2 passes vibe check; Z.ai forecasts Open Fable by December
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit buzz over Z.ai's Fable-class ambitions, An AI newsletter reports that the open model GLM-5.2 has passed community vibe checks, with Z.ai forecasting an Open Fable release by December. The piece weighs how often open-model launches fade after benchmark hype, framing GLM-5.2 as a notable exception.

entry.title: Liquid AI Introduces LFM2.5-Embedding-350M and LFM2.5-ColBERT-350M: Dense Bi-Encoder and Late-Interaction Models for Fast Multilingual Search Across 11 Languages
entry.summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-Embedding-350M and LFM2.5-ColBERT-350M, its first bidirectional retrieval models, targeting fast multilingual and cross-lingual search across 11 languages. The compact 350M models are small enough to run almost anywhere and are available on Hugging Face.

entry.title: Over-reliance on chatbots can diminish critical-thinking skills, study finds
entry.summary: A new MIT study adds to growing evidence that over-reliance on chatbots can erode users' critical-thinking skills and weaken their ability to independently detect misinformation. The research highlights a tradeoff in using AI as a fact-checking crutch.

entry.title: More people get news from AI chatbots, but trust remains low
entry.summary: The Reuters Institute's Digital News Report 2026 finds 10% of people globally now use AI chatbots for news weekly, up from 7% a year earlier, while only 4% click through to original sources and trust remains low. The data signals shifting but cautious AI news consumption habits.

entry.title: The US banned Anthropic’s Fable 5 release, but the numbers don’t seem to care

author.name: Theresa Loconsolo, Anthony Ha, Rebecca Bellan, Sean O'Kane

entry.summary: An Equity podcast covers the US government forcing Anthropic to pull Fable 5 and Mythos 5 over national security concerns after Amazon researchers allegedly bypassed Fable 5's guardrails. Critics argue the same jailbreaks exist across other models, questioning the ban's logic.

entry.title: Amazon drops its OpenAI drama film after signing a $50 billion deal with Sam Altman's company
entry.summary: Amazon MGM dropped its nearly finished OpenAI drama Artificial after Amazon struck a $50 billion partnership with OpenAI in February, with an insider saying both Altman and Musk are portrayed unfavorably. The episode raises questions about how business ties constrain creative output.

entry.title: Introducing Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Amazon made Web Search on Bedrock AgentCore generally available, giving AI agents a fully managed, MCP-compatible way to fetch live web information without provisioning search APIs or infrastructure. It addresses the limitation of agents being frozen at training time.

entry.title: Source: Elastic agrees to buy CRV-backed Deductive AI for up to $85M
entry.summary: Elastic has reportedly agreed to acquire CRV-backed Deductive AI, a three-year-old startup that uses AI to detect and resolve software bugs, for up to $85 million. The deal targets AI-driven site reliability and observability.

entry.title: Website "In the Weights" shows whether AI models know who you are
entry.summary: Two former OpenAI staff built a website called In the Weights that reveals which individuals AI models can recall from training data, scoring how deeply a person is embedded. Figures like Mozart, Shakespeare, and Taylor Swift top the strength rankings.

entry.title: The film about Sam Altman has been dropped by Amazon MGM
entry.summary: Amazon MGM has reportedly dropped Luca Guadagnino's film Artificial about Sam Altman's 2023 ouster and reinstatement, despite the project being far along with a notable cast. The studio said the film may be better served by a different distributor.

entry.title: How we built an internal data analytics agent
entry.summary: GitHub describes building Qubot, an internal Copilot-powered analytics agent that lets any employee self-serve data insights without writing queries or relying on a data analyst. The post details how AI is finally making self-serve analytics credible at scale.

entry.title: The CEO of Allbirds’ new AI biz has a plan, but no team
entry.summary: Allbirds' new AI venture reportedly has a CEO and a large seed round but no team yet, leaving its direction unclear. The story highlights the unusual structure of a single-founder, well-funded startup.

entry.title: Salesforce CodeGen Tutorial: Generate, Validate, and Rerank Python Functions With Unit Tests and Safety Checks
entry.summary: A tutorial walks through using Salesforce's CodeGen model to generate, validate, and rerank Python functions with unit tests, syntax and safety checks, and best-of-N selection. It frames CodeGen as part of a structured code-generation pipeline rather than simple completion.

entry.title: News Summary: June 19, 2026
entry.summary:
Amazon led infrastructure news, reportedly in talks to sell its in-house Trainium AI chips to external data centers—a move CEO Andy Jassy frames as a $50B opportunity directly challenging Nvidia. Separately, FERC ordered grid operators to give AI data centers a fast lane for interconnection.

  • Google DeepMind published an AI Control Roadmap treating its own agents as potential insider threats, tying security to measurable capability thresholds
  • Perplexity launched Brain, a self-improving agent memory that builds a context graph and learns overnight
  • Adobe added conversational AI agents across Photoshop, Premiere, and other Creative Cloud apps

Healthcare AI advanced sharply: two Nature studies show specialized AI matching or exceeding physicians on diagnosis and treatment, while OpenAI claims GPT-5.5 Instant now outscores doctor-written health answers.

entry.title: Amazon hopes to challenge Nvidia more directly by selling its AI chips
entry.summary: AWS is in talks to sell its in-house Trainium AI chips to external data centers, a shift CEO Andy Jassy frames as a 50 billion dollar opportunity. The move would put Amazon in more direct competition with Nvidia.

entry.title: Google Deepmind treats its own AI agents like rogue employees with office keys
entry.summary: Google DeepMind published an AI Control Roadmap that treats its own AI agents as potential insider threats, tying security measures to measurable capability levels. An analysis of one million coding tasks found most issues come from overzealous rather than malicious agents, and DeepMind warns the window for global security standards is narrowing.

entry.title: OpenAI is bringing on some big guns in the lead-up to its IPO
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion of the Shazeer departure, Ahead of a planned IPO, OpenAI hired Transformer co-inventor Noam Shazeer from Google DeepMind and former Trump AI policy official Dean Ball in the same week. The moves strengthen both its research and policy positioning.

entry.title: AI systems rival doctors in new Nature studies, but one result suggests the tech won't age well
entry.summary: Two Nature studies show specialized AI systems matching or exceeding physicians on disease diagnosis and treatment decisions in simulated cases. Notably, both systems run on already-outdated base models, hinting at rapid obsolescence.

entry.title: ChatGPT's new health upgrade beats doctor-written answers, OpenAI says
entry.summary: OpenAI upgraded ChatGPT's health capabilities via GPT-5.5 Instant, claiming it now outscores physician-written answers in accuracy, clarity, and completeness in internal tests. The company reports a 71 percent reduction in error rate for health-related statements.

entry.title: Perplexity Launches Brain, a Self-Improving Memory System That Builds a Context Graph of an Agent’s Work and Learns Overnight
entry.summary: Perplexity launched Brain, a self-improving memory system for its agent product Computer that builds a context graph of the agent's work rather than the user's preferences. At intervals such as overnight, Brain reviews the graph and teaches itself to perform tasks more efficiently, rolling out to Max and Enterprise subscribers.

entry.title: AI data centers just got a government-mandated fast lane to the grid
entry.summary: FERC directed grid operators to give AI data centers a fast lane for grid interconnection but stopped short of addressing underlying electricity supply shortages. The order prioritizes data center growth amid grid strain.

entry.title: OpenAI Releases LifeSciBench, a 750-Task Benchmark Grading AI Models on Real Life-Science Research With Expert-Written Rubric
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social announcement, OpenAI released LifeSciBench, a benchmark of 750 expert-authored life-science research tasks with grading rubrics spanning seven workflows and seven biological domains. Even the strongest models pass roughly one task in three, leaving the benchmark far from saturated.

entry.title: Bernie Sanders unveils $7 trillion plan to give Americans control of AI industry
entry.summary: Senator Bernie Sanders proposed legislation creating a sovereign wealth fund financed by a one-time 50 percent tax on the stock of the largest AI companies, targeting any firm with over 200 million dollars in annual AI sales. The estimated 7 trillion dollar fund would generate direct payments to Americans plus health, education, and housing programs.

entry.title: The White House Is Making Up Its Rules for AI in Real Time
entry.summary: Anthropic remains unable to distribute its recent Claude Mythos and Fable 5 models after running afoul of Trump administration export controls, with the specific violation still unclear. The piece highlights how AI export rules are being improvised in real time by the White House.

entry.title: AI inference startup Baseten reportedly raising $1.5B months after its last mega-round
entry.summary: AI inference startup Baseten is reportedly closing a 1.5 billion dollar round at a 13 billion dollar valuation, just months after its previous mega-round. The raise underscores intense investor appetite for inference infrastructure.

entry.title: General Intuition in talks to raise $300M at around $2B valuation
entry.summary: General Intuition is in talks to raise 300 million dollars at roughly a 2 billion dollar valuation to train embodied AI and world models. It uses Medal's dataset of around 2 billion gameplay videos per year from 10 million monthly users.

entry.title: Google's Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer joins OpenAI after two-year return stint
entry.summary: Noam Shazeer, co-author of the Attention Is All You Need paper and former Gemini co-lead, is leaving Google to join OpenAI, only about two years after returning to Google via a 2.7 billion dollar Character.AI deal. It follows Karpathy's earlier move to Anthropic as a second major talent shakeup this year.

entry.title: Using AI to help physicians diagnose rare genetic diseases affecting children
entry.summary: Researchers used an OpenAI reasoning model to assist physicians in diagnosing rare genetic diseases in children, identifying 18 new diagnoses among previously unsolved cases. The work demonstrates concrete clinical value from AI reasoning.

entry.title: Alleged China ties at SK Telecom alarmed US officials and triggered Anthropic crisis
entry.summary: Reporting indicates SK Telecom's access to Anthropic's Claude Mythos via the Project Glasswing partner program triggered the White House intervention, after US officials flagged alleged ties between the conglomerate and China. This frames the national security basis for the Anthropic export crisis.

entry.title: Who decides when AI is too dangerous?
entry.summary: A Decoder podcast discusses the US government's sudden export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 and underlying Mythos models, which restricted even foreign nationals employed by Anthropic and led the company to pull both offline. The conversation explores who decides when AI is too dangerous.

entry.title: Sound Waves Give Neuromorphic Chips a Brain-Simulating Edge
entry.summary: A new study demonstrates neuromorphic devices using sound waves to better mimic biological neurons, achieving faster and more energy-efficient operation than electronic counterparts. The approach could enable more compact and parallel neuromorphic hardware for pattern recognition and sensory tasks.

entry.title: Midjourney goes from generating cat images to full-body ultrasound scans
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Social teaser, the product is now revealed, Midjourney CEO David Holz unveiled the company's first hardware product, an ultrasound-based full-body scanner using a sensor ring to capture body composition, plus plans for a San Francisco spa to house it. He claims image quality approaching MRI for some uses.

entry.title: Improving health intelligence in ChatGPT
entry.summary: OpenAI detailed how GPT-5.5 Instant improves ChatGPT's health and wellness responses through stronger reasoning, better context handling, clearer communication, and physician-informed evaluations. It is the official writeup behind the health upgrade claims.

entry.title: Photoshop and Premiere now have AI assistants
entry.summary: Adobe launched a public beta adding bespoke conversational AI assistants to Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, and Frame.io. Each assistant is tuned to automate app-specific tasks while sharing an underlying creative agent.

entry.title: Yann LeCun warns AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic face a "big bubble explosion"
entry.summary: Yann LeCun warned that AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic face a major bubble burst, arguing their operations are investor-subsidized and operating costs are not falling fast enough. His own startup AMI Labs raised 1 billion dollars for an alternative approach.

entry.title: Midjourney, known for AI image generation, unveils a full-body ultrasound scanner and its own spa
entry.summary: Midjourney, known for AI image generation, revealed plans for a full-body ultrasound scanner and a San Francisco spa to house it. The unexpected hardware and wellness move marks a sharp departure from its core software product.

entry.title: Adobe adds AI agents to Photoshop, Premiere, and more Creative Cloud apps
entry.summary: Adobe is deploying its creative agent across major Creative Cloud apps and integrating with third-party platforms like ChatGPT and Claude. Users describe goals in natural language and the software executes multi-step creative work.

entry.title: The KV Cache Compression Race: TurboQuant vs OSCAR vs EpiCache
entry.summary: A technical overview compares emerging KV cache compression techniques TurboQuant, OSCAR, and EpiCache for long-context LLMs. It explains how the KV cache can exceed model weights at long contexts, making decoding memory-bandwidth-bound.

entry.title: Anthropic brings Artifacts to Claude Code, letting teams share live pages from coding sessions
entry.summary: Anthropic extended its Artifacts feature to Claude Code, enabling teams to turn coding session results into shareable interactive web pages. The pages auto-update from session context and maintain version history.

entry.title: A tech worker-backed PAC is bringing a $5M knife to Big Tech’s $100M gunfight
entry.summary: A tech worker-backed PAC called Guardrails is positioning as a populist counterweight to Big Tech's well-funded AI political spending, running on small donations. It enters a lopsided fight against roughly 100 million dollars in industry money.

entry.title: Prompt: The AI Race Enters Its Sovereignty Phase
entry.summary: An analysis argues the AI race is entering a sovereignty phase, with Anthropic's model restrictions exemplifying how governments and enterprises increasingly prioritize access control and AI sovereignty. The piece frames control over models as a strategic battleground.

entry.title: The Professor of Outputmaxxing — Anjney Midha, AMP
entry.summary: A Latent Space interview with Anjney Midha explores efficiency in AI scaling, highlighting that even a frontier lab like xAI may run at sub-10 percent Model FLOPs Utilization despite older runs achieving much higher MFU. It reframes the scaling debate around using existing GPUs better.

entry.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness is now generally available: Go from idea to production-grade agent in minutes
entry.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness reached general availability, providing managed infrastructure to take agents from prototype to production quickly, handling tools, sandboxed compute, storage, memory, and observability. It aims to remove the operational overhead around the agent loop.

entry.title: 3 Amazon Workers Say They’re Under Investigation for Speaking Out About Data Centers
entry.summary: Three Amazon software engineers filed a civil rights complaint alleging the company retaliated against them for testifying about data center impacts. They claim the investigation violates Seattle laws protecting political speech.

entry.title: Adobe’s redesigned AI studio remembers what your creations look like
entry.summary: Adobe is overhauling its Firefly AI studio in private beta to provide persistent context, reusable named assets, and organized cross-project workflows. The goal is to move from ideation to production without app switching.

entry.title: Amazon employees say they’re facing termination for backing data center limits
entry.summary: Three Amazon engineers say they face possible termination after testifying for a Seattle data center moratorium, with disciplinary meetings beginning days after the city council vote. They argue the action violates local political speech protections.

entry.title: Google Cloud Bets Big on the Agentic Enterprise
entry.summary: Google Cloud is centering its enterprise strategy on agentic AI, positioning autonomous agents as the core of its offerings. The piece outlines the vendor's bet on agents driving enterprise adoption.

entry.title: Snap spins off AI video team into new company, Dotmo, due to costs
entry.summary: Snap is spinning off its internal AI video team into a new independent company called Dotmo, citing cost pressures. The departing staff will focus on AI video generation outside Snap.

entry.title: MosaicLeaks: Can your research agent keep a secret?
entry.summary: A ServiceNow blog post introduces MosaicLeaks, examining whether research agents can keep secrets and avoid leaking sensitive information. It probes confidentiality risks in agent behavior.

entry.title: Is it agentic enough? Benchmarking open models on your own tooling
entry.summary: A Hugging Face post discusses benchmarking open models on users' own tooling to assess how genuinely agentic they are. It focuses on evaluating agentic competence in real workflows.

entry.title: [AINews] Midjourney Medical: scan your organs like you step on a scale
entry.summary: A newsletter recaps the Midjourney Medical launch event, debating whether it counts as AI news given the scanner itself contains no immediate AI, while noting ultrasound CT imaging needs heavy AI assistance. It captures the buzz and open questions around the device's readiness.

entry.title: Meta’s AI Workers Are Revolting, Peter Thiel’s Secret Society, and SBF’s Plea to Trump
entry.summary: A podcast episode examines dysfunction and collapsing morale inside Meta's newly formed AI unit, alongside tangential items on Peter Thiel and Sam Bankman-Fried. The focus is internal organizational turmoil rather than technical developments.

entry.title: NVIDIA SkillSpector Guide: Scanning AI Skills for Security Risks with Static Analysis and SARIF Reports
entry.summary: A tutorial demonstrates NVIDIA SkillSpector for statically analyzing AI skills for security risks before deployment, producing risk scores and SARIF reports. It walks through scanning benign and vulnerable skills and extending the framework with custom and LLM-based analysis.

entry.title: New usage analytics and updated spend controls for enterprises
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced new spend controls and usage analytics for ChatGPT Enterprise to help organizations manage costs at scale. The features target enterprise governance of AI usage.

entry.title: Monitor and debug generative AI inference with SageMaker detailed metrics and Insights dashboard on CloudWatch
entry.summary: AWS detailed new SageMaker detailed metrics and a CloudWatch Insights dashboard for monitoring and debugging generative AI inference endpoints at scale. The tools target latency, GPU memory, KV cache, and autoscaling diagnostics.
